newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel welcomes Iranian election results.
newsitem.headline: Israel welcomes Iranian election results.

text.p: Israel on Sunday welcomed presidential election results in arch-foe Iran but said it was too early to tell how they would effect the Islamic regime.

"We believe that the elections in Iran signify that the Iranian people do not want to be isolated," said David Bar-Illan, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's communications adviser, a day after the landslide victory by moderate candidate Mohammad Khatami in Iranian elections.

"We welcome this turn of events and we hope that it also means that Iran will devote its energies and its treasure to the benefit of its people rather than to develop weapons of mass destruction," he told Reuters.
Netanyahu, speaking to reporters in his office, said he hoped the development was positive but it was "too early to assess what is happening in Iran."

Khatami, 54, a senior clergyman's son and a former culture and Islamic guidance minister, is considered an open-minded religious intellectual and tolerant politician. He advocates more personal freedom, democracy and the rule of law.

Khatami crushed conservative parliament speaker Ali Akbar Nateq-Nouri who had been backed by the religious establishment that has ruled Iran since fundamentalist clerics toppled the pro-American Shah in 1979.

Israel's chief policy-maker for Lebanon, where Israel is battling Iranian-backed guerrillas, said the election results showed the force of the Islamic revolution was "waning" but Islamic clerics were still in charge.
"We must not forget that the person who makes the decisions in Iran -- unless this changes as well, and I don't see a change at this moment -- is still (supreme leader Ayatollah Ali) Khamenei."
Commercial and military ties between Israel and Iran gave way to belligerence after the 1979 revolution.

Israel accuses Tehran of developing nuclear and other non-conventional weapons to point at the Jewish state and of arming Hizbollah (Party of God) militants who battle Israeli troops in south Lebanon.
Israel also says Iran is responsible for the fate of its missing airman Ron Arad whose bomber was shot down over Lebanon in 1986. Tehran denies knowledge of his whereabouts.
